title: Vulkan Crash on Multi-GPU Linux
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible with v4.6.1.stable.mono.official

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) 13 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (nvidia) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 62.70 GiB memory

### Issue description

In a multi-GPU setup where the monitor is physically connected to the first GPU (RTX 3090), Godot defaults to using the second GPU (RTX 3080) for rendering. This caused performance issues with the UI and the mouse not clicking in the correct place in menus. 

I'm using KDE Plasma / Wayland on Debian 13. I have checked my GPU config with `vulkaninfo --summary` and the 3090 is GPU 0 / primary. 

```

GPU0:
        apiVersion         = 1.4.312
        driverVersion      = 580.126.9.0
        vendorID           = 
        deviceID           = 
        deviceType         = PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU
        deviceName         = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
        driverID           = DRIVER_ID_NVIDIA_PROPRIETARY
        driverName         = NVIDIA
        driverInfo         = 580.126.09
        conformanceVersion = 1.4.1.3
        deviceUUID         = 
        driverUUID         = 
GPU1:
        apiVersion         = 1.4.312
        driverVersion      = 580.126.9.0
        vendorID           = 
        deviceID           = 
        deviceType         = PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU
        deviceName         = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080
        driverID           = DRIVER_ID_NVIDIA_PROPRIETARY
        driverName         = NVIDIA
        driverInfo         = 580.126.09
        conformanceVersion = 1.4.1.3
        deviceUUID         = 
        driverUUID         = 
```


When attempting to force the use of the primary GPU (the 3090) via the command line argument `./Godot --gpu-index 0`, the engine fails and crashes. 
```

Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
ERROR: Condition "!present_queue_family" is true. Returning: FAILED
   at: initialize (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:7021)
WARNING: Display driver x11 failed, falling back to wayland.
     at: setup2 (main/main.cpp:3244)
WARNING: FIFO protocol not found! Frame pacing will be degraded.
     at: init (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:4872)
Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090

ERROR: Wayland protocol error 0 on interface wp_viewport@36.
   at: _poll_events_thread (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:3349)

================================================================
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 4
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.6.1.stable.mono.official (14d19694e0c88a3f9e82d899a0400f27a24c176e)
Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues
[1] /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x3fdf0) [0x7f36f6bc1df0] (??:0)
[2] /home/cowboy/Desktop/Godot/Godot() [0x4ee108] (??:0)
[3] /home/cowboy/Desktop/Godot/Godot() [0x4363eb5] (??:0)
[4] /home/cowboy/Desktop/Godot/Godot() [0x5219da3] (??:0)
[5] /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x92b7b) [0x7f36f6c14b7b] (??:0)
[6] /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x1107b8) [0x7f36f6c927b8] (??:0)
-- END OF C++ BACKTRACE --
================================================================

```


The only workaround I have that works is to launch the engine in in forced OpenGL mode like this.

`./Godot --rendering-method gl_compatibility --gpu-index 0`



### Steps to reproduce

Use the Godot Engine with two Nvidia GPUs in the computer. The engine defaults to the wrong GPU.

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25477104/mrp.zip)
